title: Professional ethics under security pressure: concept decisions 1
teachingQuestion: When professional and organizational pressure conflict, which duty controls the next authorized action?
focalInsight: Preserve facts, act within authority, and escalate an improper request through an accountable channel.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Professional Ethics
nodes.definition: Professional duties constraining security work beyond preference.
nodes.detail: Professional duties constraining security work beyond preference.
nodes.decision: Test public harm, legality, legitimate-principal service, and competence.
nodes.failureExample: A manager asks to hide a material exposure before a sale.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Identify duty and authority, then decline or escalate.

nodes.label: Public Interest
nodes.definition: Duty to consider foreseeable harm to people and society.
nodes.detail: Duty to consider foreseeable harm to people and society.
nodes.decision: Include affected people when convenience conflicts with safety.
nodes.failureExample: A known exposure is treated as only a schedule problem.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Public harm remains part of the ethical decision.

nodes.label: Competence
nodes.definition: Working within knowledge or obtaining qualified help.
nodes.detail: Working within knowledge or obtaining qualified help.
nodes.decision: Accept only work that skills or supervision support.
nodes.failureExample: An analyst approves crypto they cannot assess.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Disclose the gap and obtain review.

nodes.label: Conflict Of Interest
nodes.definition: Interest that can bias or appear to bias a decision.
nodes.detail: Interest that can bias or appear to bias a decision.
nodes.decision: Disclose before influencing selection or acceptance.
nodes.failureExample: A reviewer hides a financial interest in a supplier.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Disclosure or recusal preserves accountable judgment.

nodes.label: Responsible Disclosure
nodes.definition: Authorized, lawful reporting of material security concerns.
nodes.detail: Authorized, lawful reporting of material security concerns.
nodes.decision: Choose approved internal, legal, regulatory, or vendor route.
nodes.failureExample: Premature disclosure can expand harm, while concealment can leave a material risk unaddressed.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Use an authorized, lawful disclosure path that reduces harm and preserves accountability.

nodes.label: Scope Of Authority
nodes.definition: Limits on authorized investigation, change, or disclosure.
nodes.detail: Limits on authorized investigation, change, or disclosure.
nodes.decision: Confirm mandate, owner, and legal authority.
nodes.failureExample: An analyst searches personal accounts without authority.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Good intent does not create authority.
